title: The Ultimate Sacrifice
subtitle: Peter Collins handed over his car—and his world title—to Juan Manuel Fangio. A ghost of chivalry from an era when honor was worth more than gold.

content.text: Peter Collins was leading the championship. Fangio's car had failed. In the pits, Collins made a decision that would cost him everything and define him forever.

He stepped out. He handed over the wheel. He gave away his world title to a man who had already won four. Ferrari's court would call it honor; the points table would call it arithmetic. The gesture was tribal loyalty written in steel and petrol.
Fangio won his fifth title. Collins finished second. In the paddock, men shook hands. The sport understood that some victories are shared, some titles are earned through sacrifice.
I would have done the same for him.
content.author: Peter Collins
